record.paper_title: Complete intersection liaison and Gorenstein liaison: new results and open problems
record.context_brief: ACM schemes and Gorenstein liaison classes
record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and consider arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subschemes X of projective space P^n of fixed codimension c. Two equidimensional schemes without embedded components are in the same Gorenstein liaison class when they can be connected by a sequence of direct Gorenstein links through arithmetically Gorenstein schemes; a scheme is glicci when it lies in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection. Is there only one Gorenstein liaison class containing all arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subschemes of P^n of codimension c, equivalently are all such subschemes glicci?

evidence.quote: are all ACM subschemes X ⊂ Pn glicci?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $\mathbb{P}^n = \mathbb{P}^n_k$ be projective $n$-space. A closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ is called arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay (ACM) if its homogeneous coordinate ring $k[x_0,\dots,x_n]/I_X$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring. A subscheme is called arithmetically Gorenstein if its homogeneous coordinate ring is Gorenstein. 

Given two equidimensional closed subschemes $V_1, V_2 \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ without embedded components and of the same codimension $c$, one says that $V_1$ and $V_2$ are directly Gorenstein linked if there exists an arithmetically Gorenstein subscheme $G \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ containing both, with $I_G : I_{V_1} = I_{V_2}$ and $I_G : I_{V_2} = I_{V_1}$. The Gorenstein liaison equivalence relation is the equivalence relation generated by direct Gorenstein links. A subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ is called glicci if it lies in the same Gorenstein liaison class as some complete intersection in $\mathbb{P}^n$ of the same codimension.

Fix an integer $c \ge 1$. Is it true that every arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay closed subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of codimension $c$ is glicci, equivalently, that there is exactly one Gorenstein liaison class containing all codimension-$c$ ACM subschemes of $\mathbb{P}^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay subscheme of projective space is glicci is widely cited as a central open problem in Gorenstein liaison theory. It is known to hold in codimension 2 (where glicci is equivalent to having an N-type resolution) and for various special classes (e.g., certain monomial ideals, standard determinantal schemes), but the general case—even for zero-dimensional schemes in $\mathbb{P}^3$—remains open as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Monomial ideals and the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection
status_evidence.snippet: Shows certain monomial ideals are glicci, contributing partial progress toward the general question.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist; the general glicci question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Glicci ideals
status_evidence.snippet: Studies further classes of ideals shown to be glicci.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research treats the problem class by class without resolving it in general.

status_evidence.title: Gorenstein Liaison and ACM Sheaves
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the open problem of whether all ACM subschemes are glicci, with the lowest open-dimensional case being zero-schemes in P^3.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as open; the lowest-dimensional unresolved case is zero-dimensional schemes in P^3.
